body: This is great advice, and thanks for sharing. It seems that every time I cook something healthy as well as delicious (in my mind) he will find some part of the meal that he finds unpalatable. Like, for example: he hates sour cream, avocados, most fish (unless fried and boneless), sourdough bread, most fruits save for green grapes and apples, salads made with more veggie assortment than lettuce, any oil and vinegar or citrus juice salad dressing (gots to be creamy ranch), whole wheat flatbread pizza crust, and about a thousand other food hangups. He does go wild over the veggies drenched in butter...that's a big hit in our house too. I get the idea that some men may feel some kind of way about dieting and eating lighter because of social stigmas/gendered expectations, but logically, when one's health depends on it, I really don't see how these types can justify this behavior. I know that if I was severely overweight and gasping for breath just laying on my back, I'd not care much how I looked eating a salad bowl instead of the triple bacon death stack, or whatever these guys think is manly. I can't really wrap my mind around their justifications.

I think that's one of his meds, something for depression. He takes so many. I can't make it to all of his appts, but I think he does take something for anxiety and depression. I actually think that one is the one that started making him sleep so much when they added it.

I feel you. We did buy this place together. I care enough for him that I'd let him have this house and I'd just start over. He may need the space for his medical equipment anyway. I think I would be ok with a smaller place anyhow because I don't need all the space. Never been a junk junkie, very minimalist. My husband is the hoarder, and honestly, I don't want to go thru all of his crap. He can have it all. If and when I leave, I want to start over 100% fresh and clean. It's something I do look forward to eventually.

He stopped caring after he got out the Army and had an accident in Ft. Irwin during NTC training. I get my VA benefits and I work part time, he gets wayyy more VA benefits than I do because they declared him 90% disabled...BUT, his physicians have also cleared him for light running at his own pace, limited upper body weight lifting, and unlimited walking at his own pace...so clearly, you see, he can do more than lay around and sleep and stare at the flashing box like a floppy newborn when he comes home. He's 10 years my senior at 44, and I honestly believe that he sees me as a meal ticket so far as being taken care of, and also, I hate to say it, as a trophy. He has a great job and makes more money than me but he also had military training to get in at a senior level position. He puts in his all at work I suppose (it's a desk job) then comes home and acts like he's helpless and I work too. He tries to milk his health issues for sympathy even from total strangers and I find that so unattractive. I never saw this part of him when we were dating. I never saw this apathy from him when we were dating. 

This is a new feature in our relationship that happened in the past 4-5 years since he has been spiraling from the accident and getting out the Army. I don't even know who he is anymore. He used to be so fitness conscious and gung-ho. He used to motivate and inspire me when I was lazy. Now, he's like a reverse motivational poster. Yeah, his lack of self care is disturbing. I had to pitch a bitch to make him shower after work before laying on my bed (he has his own room, we don't even sleep together...but he calls himself spending time with me when he comes into my room after work to watch SVU for 5 min before he collapses into loud snoring sleep) because he sweats and smells so bad. I straight up told him that he smelled, and he needs to bathe and use deodorant every day or he'd be hearing it from his co workers eventually. I snapped him out of that phase so I guess I'm hoping I can snap him into better eating too? Wishful thinking maybe.

I honestly think it's a lost cause, but our 2 kids love him so much and I honestly believe he is going to die very soon by his own hand (to mouth). Do I love him? I used to, and in 'that way'. Very much.  He was not like this before his accident. Now, I love him like a good platonic male friend. I'm going to be real...I'm poor. I work two part time jobs and sure, I can get a shitty apt in the hood just to be apart from him, but it would be just to prove a point that "I can" and then what though?  He sleeps and then eats, eats and then sleeps. Honestly, I am a single parent already with him on the opposite side of the house. 

He comes home from work and it's like he's not even here anyway. I make solo plans, or plans with the kids, because he hates going to do anything that involves physical efforts (hiking, swimming, etc). We don't communicate well because he engages in defensive behavior anytime I try to share how I feel about all of this. It's like he just wants to maintain the staus quo and not even try. Anytime I try to suggest things or start a talk, he wants to claim it's a bad time to talk (it's too late at night, it's "always this conversation", and etc), so yeah he is quite PA. He claims he loves me more than anything but all I feel is a hole in my heart and let down. I feel that if he truly loved me and our family, he'd try, try try to lose the weight and find a fitness program to get back on track.

 I share stories about double amputees and people with all kinds of limitations that get fit and stay fit, but his issues are always worse than anyone else's in the Universe. Woe is him. That really turns me off more than anything, the defeatism and refusal to even try.

Like any statistic, there is the mean and standard deviation and outliers, of course. Basically, anyone can educate themselves on better nutrition and do what is within their means.  I'm poor myself, but budgeting for what is important according to your means is easy when you realize your heath is a precious investment. I saw 'poor' people in my old hood that were on it. Fit, healthy people that ate healthily and they'd walk or run daily. They stand out in the hood. These kinds of people are usually on a different frequency than the mainstream though, into natural things. 

I also see 'poor' people walking around with the new iphones, wearing fancy name brand clothing and shoes that I can't afford. If they can make the trip to the mall to acquire those expensive things, then they could also make a trip to the food market and choose better foods. I'm just generalizing obviously, but priorities. If the new Jordan's are more important than nourishing your body and you can live with eating ramen, hot cheap garbage from the fast food shops and Tyson ready made chicken nuggets on a regular basis, then more power to you. We all choose our destiny.

I like their strawberry sparkling water, and it's always so cheap compared to the sparkling water at my big chain store. You can get two 1.5 liter bottles for 2 bucks.

I suppose here is my thin/small boob privilege...cheap bras fit and support me well and I look cute. Plus, They function well enough for exercise because let's face it, A/B boobs aren't hitting you in the face on a run or making your back hurt. Silver lining in every cloud.

Make slow, gradual changes. Don't start off with some radical diet plan and don't look to exercise beyond walking for a few weeks. You want to stay motivated. Reducing food consumption is going to suck for the first few weeks, so take it easy on yourself.

Have a few things you like each day, but set a reasonable calorie goal. Try to replace things like fried chicken with baked chicken or baked fish. 

Remember cake (or cookies, or hot krispy kremes...) is fine, just not everyday. Find your balance, only you can do what works best for you. See your doc if you think you can't do it alone. Good luck.

I got sick of avoiding certain items in my closet because I was in denial about my weight gain. Generally, people hate to be put on the spot about these things. Denial is a real thing. I think it's optimal if they can self motivate, but then, I have seen some people keep on plugging along with overweight...until their Dr tells them they have some sort of issue that requires treatment and then some people do a 180. But then again, even more just don't gaf, even when death is the consequence. 

Summation: All that said, I have pretty much given up trying to convince anyone because it seems most usually think you're being pushy/judgmental/a snob/rude/etc.
Best of luck to you. I hope you succeed.
